question:
A beta particle (electron) is emitted with kinetic energy $K=2.0\,\text{MeV}$.

(a) Find its de Broglie wavelength using the relativistic relation

$$pc=\sqrt{K(K+2m_ec^2)},\qquad \lambda=\frac{hc}{pc},$$

with $m_ec^2=0.511\,\text{MeV}$ and $hc=1240\,\text{eV\,nm}$.

(b) A typical nuclear radius is $R\approx 5\,\text{fm}=5\times10^{-6}\,\text{nm}$. Estimate the minimum kinetic energy $K_{\min}$ an electron must have so that its de Broglie wavelength becomes $\lambda\approx R$. (You may use $K\approx pc$ for $pc\gg m_ec^2$)
